absent: How the core attribute walk splits, preserves, or collapses large pages and when it allocates.
Ordering and scope guarantees of translation cache flushes and cache writebacks.
Memory type reservation conflict rules and lifetime outside the shown call sites.
Implementation of generic address lookup, fixmap slots, and page frame conversions.
Consumer logic for the fault prefix and opcode tables and resulting actions.
Protection key programming and encrypted memory adjustment formulas.
Maintenance sites for direct mapping counters and large page enablement.
Page table descriptor allocation failure paths and list synchronization beyond shown helpers.

findings.text: Request descriptor holds progress in curpage against numpages with a pfn, plus protection deltas in mask_set and mask_clr, plus a vaddr slot and optional pgd and pages references, plus a flags word with single bit requests force_split and force_static_prot and force_flush_all and init_mm_read_locked.

Four one bit attributes shorted and enlarged and rexr and rex record decoded prefix effects for faulting instruction analysis, distinguishing operand size override, address size override, extended register selection, and presence of an extended prefix byte.
A file private spinlock exists to provide mutual exclusion around the attribute change path.
Kernel page directory instances are tracked on a global list with their owning address space recorded, and removal from that list happens while holding a dedicated directory lock.

Per level counters track how many direct mapping pages exist at each size, and the memory information reporting converts those counts to kilobytes with level appropriate scaling, selecting a two megabyte versus four megabyte label based on build configuration and showing a one gigabyte line only when that size is enabled.

Monotonic counters record how many large and small pages were examined, left unchanged, preserved, or installed during attribute changes, and a debug file exposes those counters through sequential file operations with open, read, seek and release handling.

A sixteen entry table indexed by combinations of read, write, execute and shared flags yields the initial page protection, mapping private writable combinations to copy on write variants, shared writable combinations to shared variants, execute combinations to executable variants, and empty or shared only combinations to inaccessible.

Derivation of page protection from virtual memory flags masks to the four basic permission bits, then overlays memory protection key bits when configured, applies encrypted memory adjustment, and finally intersects with the supported protection mask whenever the result is present.

New top level directories inherit kernel entries by cloning the kernel portion except on builds that preallocate all lower directories, and each new directory records its owner and joins the global synchronization list.

Preallocation offers all or nothing semantics with accounting balanced against freeing, using user page table allocation without high memory and without charging the initial address space, and freeing tolerates sparse arrays while releasing each present descriptor and adjusting counts.
A read only after init physical address mask covers exactly the supported physical bits as derived from the configured shift.

Uncached and write combining transitions on contiguous kernel ranges first reserve the requested memory type over the corresponding physical span and only on success apply the attribute change, releasing the reservation if the change fails; writeback does the reverse order by applying first and releasing only on success.

Array based cache changes skip high memory pages for reservation bookkeeping, funnel write combining through an intermediate uncached minus step before final conversion, clear all cache bits when returning to writeback before releasing reservations, and unwind any reservations already taken when a later reservation or the attribute change itself fails.

Direct map validity helpers set or clear present plus writable state without alias checking, and the debug page allocation path uses those helpers with a debug flag followed by a local only full flush under disabled preemption plus lazy mode draining.

Middle directory lookup walks down from the kernel top level and yields absence when any upper level is empty, non present, or already a leaf, otherwise returning the middle entry for the address; virtual to physical translation selects the base frame according to the reported level and combines it with the offset within that level.

Reporting, persistent memory invalidation, and cache invalidation are available as architecture entry points, with cache region invalidation reporting unsupported under a hypervisor and otherwise performing a system wide writeback invalidate, while internal flush helpers either flush everything with an optional cache writeback on capable processors or flush each changed kernel page individually.

Permission helpers adjust present, executable, read only executable, global and non global state over kernel ranges, with executable restoration becoming a no operation when the processor lacks the no execute feature; machine check isolation marks a frame not present through a non canonical alias except for platform pages, with a complementary helper restoring presence via the normal direct address.

Single page and contiguous page helpers forward to the range based uncached, writeback and present query operations using the kernel direct address, and boot time unmapping clears present and writable state in a caller supplied top directory without alias checking followed by a full flush.
Top level page table allocation for user address spaces forwards to the generic single page allocator with user page table funding.

Option flags CPA_FLUSHTLB and CPA_ARRAY and CPA_PAGES_ARRAY and CPA_NO_CHECK_ALIAS and CPA_COLLAPSE and CPA_DEBUG_PAGEALLOC take decimal values one, two, four, eight, sixteen and thirty two in that order.
BIOS_PFN and BIOS_PFN_END are frame numbers derived by rounding down the start and the inclusive end of the firmware reserved range.
Warning kinds CPA_CONFLICT and CPA_PROTECT and CPA_DETECT are ordered from zero upward, with the compiled default selecting the middle protection level.

Reason labels NOT_ME and NOTHING and REG_READ and REG_WRITE and IMM_WRITE and OTHERS distinguish outside region, inside but unrelated, register read, register write, immediate write and unhandled cases; instruction classification uses tables of legacy prefixes and opcode groups for read versus write and for access width, with a sixty four bit variant adding the full extended prefix range and moving wide memory operations to a separate width class.

Low register encodings map zero through seven to the classic accumulator through destination byte and word families, with sixty four bit builds extending eight through fifteen to the additional registers.

PREALLOCATED_PMDS and PREALLOCATED_USER_PMDS and MAX_PREALLOCATED_USER_PMDS are zero on builds without the extension requiring them, otherwise covering all top entries plus a protection isolation dependent user count capped at the kernel portion size.

Virtual to physical translation traps when no mapping exists, cache region invalidation warns and fails when the feature is unavailable, boot time unmapping warns if secondary processors are already online, machine check isolation depends on physical address sanitization of its decoy and logs on failure, and the debug mapping path leaves remote translation caches stale by design with faults expected to self heal.
